root_idea.summary: The root centers on stirring up or disturbing what covers a thing so that it can be uncovered or sought.
root_idea.development: The semantic development runs from scraping or stirring earth by hand to seeking what is hidden, and then to inquiry, investigation, and examination.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To scrape or dig in the earth in search of, or to uncover, something.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction بَحَثَ فِي الأَرْضِ, the action is physical scraping or digging through the ground. The occurrence does not by itself establish the broader abstract sense of investigating a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To search for something or seek information about it; to inquire into, investigate, scrutinize, or examine a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction بَحَثَ عَنْهُ denotes searching or inquiring about something, while بَحَثَ فِيهِ can denote investigating or examining it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Searching, inquiry, investigation, scrutiny, or examination.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Verbal noun of بَحَثَ in its abstract searching and investigating uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To investigate or examine a matter with another, especially through disputation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal interaction may involve scrutinizing one another's secrets or faults and exchanging accusations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To inquire into one another's secrets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction referring to mutual investigation of concealed matters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To play with dust or earth, especially in the game called البُحْثَةُ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form VIII usage associated with a dust-playing game.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mine in which gold or silver is sought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun referring to a place where prospecting is conducted.
The designation is explained by the serpent's scraping up dust or earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A game played with dust or earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The spelling البَحْثَةُ is also reported for this game.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels that scrape up dust or earth with their forefeet while walking, throwing it behind them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet describing this characteristic manner of movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intensive epithet for one who probes or investigates; also a traditional name of Surat al-Tawbah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The surah name is explained by its probing into the hypocrites and their secrets; variant vocalization البُحُوثُ is also reported for the surah title.
Reported in the proverbial expression بَدَا بَحِيثُهُمْ, “their secret became apparent.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dust or earth scraped up from the thing being searched in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the material displaced during searching or digging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who scrapes up dust or earth, or one who searches.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In proverbial comparisons, the term can describe someone whose search leads to his own destruction, as in the search for the buried knife.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The dust or earth gathered by a jerboa in its burrow.
A place or time of scraping, digging, searching, inquiring, investigating, scrutinizing, or examining.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural مَبَاحِثُ; the noun can cover either a physical or an investigative setting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A remote, desolate, or unknown place where a person’s whereabouts are not known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This specialized meaning occurs in the expression تَرَكْتُهُ بِمَبَاحِثِ البَقَرِ.

cautions: The sole Quran occurrence, 5:31, denotes physical scraping or digging in the earth; abstract inquiry and investigation are broader Classical Arabic uses.
The sense “secret” for بَحِيثٌ is reported with a citation disagreement in the lexical evidence.
